clue.text: Garment paid for on receipt in Massachusetts

definitions.note: a location phrase standing for a place found there

blocks.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak
COD stands for cash on delivery, payment made when goods arrive

explanation.surface: Someone buys clothing in Massachusetts and pays when the parcel turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is unusually loose: 'in Massachusetts' stands for a place that lies in that state.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooked peninsula in the American north-east is one of the best-known features of that New England state.

clue.text: Want a little time

blocks.note: something little is short
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone asks for just a few moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as a verb asking for something, but it is the noun meaning lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack or insufficiency is a synonym for a scarcity of supply.

clue.text: Liquor to drink up: result - uproar

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: rum is a spirit
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Drinking spirits ends, predictably, in a noisy brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or commotion, the same as an uproar.

clue.text: Soldier employed by the navy

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a warship

blocks.note: first meaning: an old term for a fighting man or warrior
second meaning: an armed sailing warship

explanation.surface: A soldier is seconded to serve with the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated phrase once meant a warrior, and later named a heavily armed sailing vessel of the fleet.

clue.text: New fears about opening the attack

indicators.note: something new is remade, so these letters come out in fresh order
about means placed around, so one piece wraps the other
the opening of a word is its initial letter only

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fresh worries surround the start of an offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: One point is needed to beat the old club

blocks.note: a nib is the single point of a pen
to lick is informally to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: A single point is all that's required to defeat a long-established sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a sports team, but it is a golf club: the niblick was the old name for a lofted iron, roughly a nine-iron.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a traditional golf iron with a steeply angled face, now superseded by numbered irons.

clue.text: Give generously when there's a whip-round?

definitions.text: Give generously when there's a whip-round?

blocks.clueFragment: Give generously when there's a whip-round?
blocks.note: surface reading: donating freely when colleagues pass round a collection
setter's reading: whipping round suggests striking out with a lash, which is also the idiom for spending lavishly

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to be generous when the office collection comes round.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip-round is a British informal collection of money among a group; the phrase meaning spend freely also literally means strike with a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to spend money freely or extravagantly, as well as to hit out violently.

clue.text: Flier in a flat spin

indicators.note: a spin sends things whirling, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is panicking, in a flat spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a flat spin' is a British idiom for agitated panic; here the phrase splits into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantail is a breed of domestic pigeon with a spread tail, or a small flycatcher bird, either way a winged creature.

clue.text: One whose meteoric career is almost over

definitions.text: One whose meteoric career is almost over

blocks.clueFragment: One whose meteoric career is almost over
blocks.note: surface reading: a celebrity whose rapid rise is about to end
setter's reading: taken literally, an actual meteor streaking across the sky before burning out

explanation.surface: A celebrity who shot to fame is now on the way down.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting meteor seen in the night sky is popularly called this, and the phrase also describes a fading celebrity.

clue.text: Pot red by mistake - it's too much!

indicators.note: a mistake puts things in the wrong order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A snooker player sinks the red accidentally and is told that's overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: Potting a red is a snooker shot. The answer is a French phrase used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: The borrowed French expression means superfluous or unwanted, literally excessive in number.

clue.text: Lovely girl, outwardly competent

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: able means capable
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A charming young woman who is capable on the face of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone delightful and easy to love or admire.

clue.text: It may be produced by carbon monoxide to a degree

definitions.text: It may be produced by carbon monoxide to a degree

blocks.note: CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A gas leak can bring on a medical condition to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, since poisoning by this gas can cause unconsciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of deep prolonged unconsciousness, which serious carbon monoxide poisoning can bring on.

clue.text: Newcastle is set round a river - a great seaway

indicators.note: to set something is to arrange it, so these letters are put in new order
round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go about another piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An English city is described as built around a river, a major waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American river and its seaway link the Great Lakes to the Atlantic for ocean shipping.

clue.text: One regarding the nineties as a thing of the past

definitions.text: One regarding the nineties as a thing of the past

blocks.clueFragment: One regarding the nineties as a thing of the past
blocks.note: surface reading: someone dismissing the 1990s decade as old history
setter's reading: the nineties of a person's age, which a hundred-year-old has left behind

explanation.surface: Someone views a recent decade as already passé.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has reached a hundred years old has lived beyond their own nineties.

clue.text: Russian comrade

blocks.note: surface reading: a fellow party member in Russia
setter's reading: the Russian-language word itself for comrade

explanation.definitionFit: This is the Russian word used as a form of address meaning comrade, especially in Soviet times.

clue.text: Roman water-carrier

blocks.note: surface reading: a person in ancient Rome who fetched water
setter's reading: a structure that channels water across country

explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Rome built long bridge-like channels to convey water supplies into its cities.

clue.text: English queen, one with real potential

indicators.note: potential describes what could become something else, so these letters may form a new word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A queen of England is described as having genuine promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the two parts of the fodder. Eleanor of Aquitaine and Eleanor of Castile were both queens of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Several medieval consorts of English kings bore this name, notably the wives of Henry II and Edward I.

clue.text: Produced admitted  superiority

blocks.note: first meaning: gave forth, as a field gives a crop
second meaning: gave way to a stronger opponent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Produced' looks like it governs the next words, but the clue splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both bearing a crop or return and giving way or surrendering to another.

clue.text: Unwise profession of medical consultant

definitions.note: a cryptic description, read as two words

blocks.note: first meaning: badly judged
second meaning, read as two words: a consultant's job is to counsel sick patients

explanation.surface: A doctor's line of work is said to be foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as ILL ADVISED, the answer describes sick people being given advice, which is what a consultant does.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adjective means foolish or imprudent, acting on poor judgement.

clue.text: In which the early bird lies awaiting the worm?

definitions.text: In which the early bird lies awaiting the worm?

blocks.clueFragment: In which the early bird lies awaiting the worm?
blocks.note: surface reading: the proverb about early risers catching worms
setter's reading: a morning bird lurking in a shrub, a hidden position from which to spring on prey

explanation.surface: A bird gets up early and waits to catch a worm.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AM BUSH, the answer is a morning shrub where the early bird might hide, as well as a surprise attack from cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise attack launched from a concealed position, exactly how a lurking predator waits for prey.

clue.text: Murder mother for the estate

blocks.note: to do in is slang for to kill
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone kills their mother to inherit the property.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no container signal: the slang phrase for kill is simply split around the word for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is lands or territory owned or ruled by someone, like an estate.

clue.text: Single piece of ammunition

indicators.note: a piece of something is just part of it, so the letters lie inside the next word

blocks.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.surface: One bullet or cartridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single individual thing, one complete item counted on its own.

clue.text: Australian capital ship

blocks.note: first meaning: the seat of Australia's federal government
second meaning: a warship or liner bearing the name, such as the P&O liner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital ship' is a naval term for a major warship, which hides the split between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the national capital, and several naval vessels and a famous cruise liner bore the same name.

clue.text: Posers seldom resolved

indicators.note: something resolved is worked out anew, so these letters are sorted into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Puzzles that are rarely solved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posers' suggests difficult problems, but here it means people who pose.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists' sitters and fashion mannequins strike poses for painters or photographers.

clue.text: Legendary bird returns, so it is written, to a Mediterranean isle

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird
sic is Latin for thus, used to flag a quotation copied exactly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mythical bird flies back to an island, according to the written record.
explanation.definitionFit: The French island lies in the Mediterranean Sea north of Sardinia and was Napoleon's birthplace.

clue.text: Company of high-fliers

blocks.note: surface reading: a firm of ambitious, successful executives
setter's reading: people literally flying high, the staff of an aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: The pilots and cabin staff working aboard an aeroplane form a team that flies at altitude.
